$comment: The step result cache and the affected-only release (docs/GATES.md "Affected-only releases"). Hand-written policy; tools/step-inputs.json is the derived input map (tools/step-inputs.mjs). Read by the runner only (no gate driver reads this file, so editing it never changes a step's inputs).

runnerKey.$comment: The runner code that changes how every step runs or what its cache entry claims (its environment, timeouts, kills, hosts, splits, the tracer, the coverage collector and the key itself): its blobs are in every key, so a change to any of them re-runs everything. The fail audit found 8 past FAILs only a runner change explains.

classes.$comment: Input classes: globs (a leading ! excludes). A step's input set is the union of its classes, its drivers' module closure, the globs that closure needs and the data its traced runs read.

classRules.$comment: Which classes a step gets: by its client (any game client, `self` included), by a gradle cwd, by modules in its closure (a driver that talks to a game, or runs gradle in the source checkout). A closure module that spawns node with a fresh environment (env: { PATH: ... }: the child runs untraced) adds untracedNode.

derived.$comment: Untracked paths a step may read that are built from tracked inputs: the trace allows them, and the key carries the tracked files they derive from (globs).

fingerprint.$comment: Untracked inputs hashed by content when a key is computed (local data that is not in git).

state.$comment: Untracked run-time state a step reads in its run worktree or the source checkout: the game dir, logs, scratch. Not an input (the worlds a step restores are fingerprinted from the snapshot store; what a base step creates comes from code).

external.$comment: Files a step read under the main checkout's artifacts/ (archived tag builds, apitest jars): fingerprinted (size, mtime) into its cache entry and re-checked at every lookup. These are caches keyed by content, or a run's own evidence: ignored.

uncacheable.$comment: Steps never served from the cache (their PASS is not recorded): fresh-seed fuzz, inputs outside git that the key can't see, probes that read other steps' evidence of the same run.
uncacheable.umt-long: fresh clock seeds every run: the point is new seeds
uncacheable.apijars: runs the archived apitest jars under artifacts/ (outside git)
uncacheable.6b-versionc: runs an archived release jar (outside git)
uncacheable.p3-probe-water: reads h-ingame, hy-ingame and h-probe's evidence of the same run
uncacheable.p3-probe-ledger: reads y-ingame and cu-survival's evidence of the same run
uncacheable.p2-calibration: a calibration probe: always runs at release

modeEnv.$comment: The environment that changes what a step runs: every variable a module of its closure reads (process.env.NAME), every ambient variable with the project's prefixes (prefixes: the JVM, the sidecar, the client scripts and aliased reads are invisible to the scan), plus always; less the per-run plumbing (ports, run and out dirs, tokens; a *_DIR that redirects an input, such as ARCHITECT_STAMPS_DIR or LINT_KIT_DIR, is a mode).

nightly.$comment: The full twins only the nightly runs (Noah, 2026-10-23; docs/GATES.md "Smoke at releases"). A release replaces each by its smoke or slice twin (tiers.release.always names the twin) and never runs the full id, wherever the selection got it from (the always list, an impact rule, --full). The nightly (release --full --nightly, tools/nightly.mjs) adds every id here; the twin it supersedes then drops (supersededBy). p3-probe-water reads the full h-ingame, hy-ingame and h-probe evidence of its run, so it runs with them in the nightly; p3-probe-ledger (y-ingame, cu-survival) stays in the release. Not here: irr-ingame, c29-ingame, voc-survival, x-resume, 6a-eflat, 6a-staged and c30, whose smoke saves almost nothing.

release.$comment: The release tier's selection (docs/GATES.md "Affected-only releases", "Benches out of the release path"). Candidates: tiers.release.always, the rotation, and every step an impact rule names (change and slice lists), the supersededBy twins and the judged benches (benches.judged) dropped. A candidate runs when its key misses, when it is a canary, or when it is a full twin whose last PASS is older than the last full nightly. The judged benches are decided by the bench rule (benches below): the latest nightly's PASS is reused unless what the bench measures changed since.

canaries.$comment: always: the calibration probes, every release. scenarioRotation: one big scenario per release by the rotation key (a cache spot-check: it runs even when cached; at a release that is not the nightly its timing is recorded, not judged). crashRotation: the crash suite the tier's rotation picks. The judged benches are no longer canaries (2026-10-22): the bench rule decides them.

benches.$comment: The judged benches (Noah, 2026-10-22; docs/GATES.md "Benches out of the release path"; tools/lib/bench-select.mjs). judged: the benches whose timing is judged; they are not release candidates. The nightly (tools/nightly.mjs: release --full --nightly) runs them isolated with their timing judged and records their PASSes in the step cache (only the nightly's: a contended or recorded-timing PASS never serves). A release reuses each bench's latest nightly result when it was a PASS, its step-cache entry still holds at HEAD (its coverage or input set, definition, toolchain, runner and modes) and no path of a sensitive group naming it changed between the nightly's head and HEAD (git diff, two-dot); otherwise the release runs it, the reason in --plan. megaB is one bench of two walks: the release runs the full walk when its sensitive paths changed, else the fast one. nightlyOnly: never run at release. nightlyJudged: the scenarios, ordinary cache candidates at release with their timing recorded there; only the nightly judges it. megaB: the nightly runs the full walk on weeklyDay (the nightly's local start day, about 02:00), on demand (nightly.mjs --megab-full), when no nightly has run it yet, and when a sensitive group naming it changed since the last full walk; the fast walk otherwise. sensitive: the bench-sensitive paths (PROPOSED 2026-10-22 for the coordinator's review), by group, each with the benches it re-runs.

placement core.why: the per-tick placement budget, the jobs that write and restore cells, the batch and group loops, the journal they write: every bench's own tick, cells/s and undo

block-write queue.why: the queue that feeds the writes and holds the chunk tickets: megaA's liveness, held-ticket wait and starvation bars

region tiles.why: the region's tile stream, its wire format and the realised record: megaA's wire bytes/cell, tile latency and cells/s

scheduler.why: what runs in the server tick beside the writes, and the trace the tick bars read

sidecar tile path.why: the sidecar side of a tile: the region pool, its worker and the kit CLI it runs

autoFull.$comment: --full is the rule when the release range matches: the Minecraft version or a build dependency (mod/build.gradle, settings, the wrapper, gradle.properties beyond mod_version), or a path of the engine list (PROPOSED 2026-10-22, awaiting the coordinator's approval): the journal and its store (journal/**), the block-write queues (batch/**, site/RegionQueue, TickDeferral, ChunkTickets), the placement and removal core (site/TemplateWriter, PlaceJob, RestoreJob, InfraJob, SiteJournal, Sites, Groups, Batches, Placement; placement/Reconcile; region/RegionsImpl), the files the UMT rule names as undo-critical (site/FluidRearm, TileCheck, LotMask; not region/RegionFluids, which the coordinator ruled not engine), placement tracking (placed/**) and the world-update mixins (mixin/**, the mixins json). kit/lib/** no longer forces it: kit changes run what their coverage says.

release.evidenceDeps: a canary or a running step whose waitFor target (other than unit-kit, whose JUnit report a cached run hands on) reads that step's evidence of the same run: the target runs too

nightly.$comment: tools/nightly.mjs: release --full --no-cache on a fresh detached origin/main, in its own worktree and run dirs. extraArgs: added to the gate-run command (--turbo: the run waits for the whole machine and holds it, docs/GATES.md "Turbo"). idleWaitMin: when a gate run is active or queued at start, how long to wait for an idle machine (no queue ticket taken) before skipping the night; 0 (the brief): exit at once. yieldAfter (local time): past it, with another run queued, the turbo run yields (SIGUSR2: nothing new starts, its running steps finish) and the steps it didn't start run as a one-slot run; the summary records the yield.

coverage.$comment: Coverage-based inputs (tools/lib/step-coverage.mjs, docs/GATES.md "Coverage-based inputs"): an in-game step (a class in replaces) records what its run touched (its JVMs' loaded classes, its and its client's node files) and caches against that set plus `always` (and the closures of alwaysRoots) instead of the whole-tree classes. A compile-time constant changed in Java invalidates every coverage PASS.

why.mixins: applied to their targets as bytes by the mixin transformer: never loaded under their own name
why.registries, codecs, serialization, nbt: read world and save data whose shape a run may not exercise, and register at startup
why.devserver: generated hooks (build-time code from the client's hook sources) and the headless host: small, always in
why.sidecar/src: one esbuild bundle: loading it loads all of it
why.kit tools and data the sidecar spawns: the sidecar spawns kit tools with minimalEnv (no NODE_OPTIONS: untraced): their closures are in alwaysRoots; the region CLI runs under Node's permission model, where no tracer can load, so a step that planned (the sidecar's stat of kit/tools/region.mjs) gets the CLI's closure and every region program (whenTouched); plan.mjs itself is always in (the KIT_INFO probe reads its constants)
why.region worker: traced: the tracer's Worker wrapper loads it first and passes its environment even to a worker given env: {} (the region pool); kept in for safety

whenTouched.$comment: Conditional safety: when a run's traces show the trigger (path and kind), the step also gets these roots' closures and globs. The sidecar plans regions by spawning kit/tools/region.mjs under Node's permission model, untraced (the tracer can't load inside that sandbox); runKit stats the script first (kind s), so that stat marks a step that planned. kit/test/step-cache.test.mjs guards that contract in sidecar/src/regions.ts.

build.$comment: The run-level build artifact (tools/lib/build-artifact.mjs): the classes of mod (main, client, test), devserver and apitest, compiled once per hash of these inputs in the worktree below, offline, with a manifest of every class file's digest in artifacts/build-cache/<hash>.json. A coverage-mode key holds the bytecode digests of the classes its run loaded; a failed or missing build means no coverage lookup.
